The MRI of right knee without IV adminstration of contrast medium is performed with the pulse sequences - sagittal T1, PD+FS, and T2+FS, axial T2+FS and coronal T2+FS. 

The MR images reveal: 

> Osteoarthric change of right knee. Grossly preserved joint space and alignment. 
> PD hyperintensities are detected in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. More in favor of medial meniscus degenerative tear.
> Presence of PD hyperintensities in the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), probably secondary to the posttraumatic injury or chronic inflammation. 
> Subchondral erosions, subcortical cysts, and cartilage thinning at the lateral patellofemoral joint. Osteoarthritis and advanced chondromalacia is favored. 
> The continuity and alignment of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) are preserved. 
> Normal joint effusion. 
> The lateral meniscus is intact without tear. 
> Presence of some fluid collection in the infrapatellar bursa. 
> Presence of a small hyperintensity in the upper portion of the patella, reflecting a focal tendinitis. 
> Subcutaneous edematous infiltration is detected at anterior knee. In favor of inflammation. 
> The medial and lateral collateral ligaments, iliotibial tract, quadriceps tendon, and other structures are intact without definite abnormalities by this knee MR examination. 

<Impressions> : 
1) Osteoarthric change of right knee. 
2) PD hyperintensities are detected in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. More in favor of medial meniscus degenerative tear. 
3) Presence of PD hyperintensities in the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), probably secondary to the posttraumatic injury or chronic inflammation. 
4) Subchondral erosions, subcortical cysts, and cartilage thinning at the lateral patellofemoral joint. Osteoarthritis and advanced chondromalacia is favored. 
5) Presence of some fluid collection in the infrapatellar bursa. 
6) Presence of a small hyperintensity in the upper portion of the patella, reflecting a focal tendinitis.
[ID]. In favor of inflammation. 

Recommend clinical correlation and Orthopedics consultation for further evaluation and management.

MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS


* Status of  lateral subluxation of patella
Laxity of medila patellar retinaculum with mild increased singnal intensity, R/O grade 2 injury.
* Massively increased joint effusion and extending to proximal tibiofibular joint with hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis;  Prominent suprapatellar bursitis  ; suprapatellar and medial plicae.
* The patellar length/ patellar tendon length =0.65 (<0.8) in this study; suspicious of  high riding patella.
* Mild fat stranding along proximal portion of patellar tendon and infrapatellar fat plane, maybe due to inflammation or post arthrocentesiis change.
Increased signal intensity of articular cartilage at lateral facet, R/O grade 1 chondromalacia.
* Tiny subchondral cysts in tibial eminence
* Increased infiltration in the muscle of popliteus muscle and intermuscular infiltration(srs:[ID], Img:24; srs:6001, Img:26), R/O mild myositis 

Impression: 
1.  Synovitis of knee joint with massive joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis, R/O post-trumatic arthritis or inflammatory arthritis or infection. Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and lab data.
2. Status of lateral subluxation of patella, R/O grade 2 injury of medial patellar retinaculum.
3. High riding patella in this study but no significant evidence of full thickness tear of patellar tendon.
4. In favor of grade 1 patellar chondromalacia.
5. R/O mild myositis of popliteus muscle.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management
